A per-server approve/reject list IS applied to exactly these records one layer above the cited files.

1. QUOTE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md` line 272: "Automatically approve all MCP servers defined in project `.mcp.json` files." (followed by a v2.1.196 clause). `disabledMcpjsonServers` at :263, `enabledMcpjsonServers` at :274. Confirmed.

2. A full `grep -rna` (NUL-safe, no --include filters) over the repo finds the three identifiers in NO source file — only in `docs/architecture/unified-plugin-adapter-runtime.md:198` prose and the sweep's own JSON. 3. ONE LAYER UP — REFUTES THE CONSEQUENCE. `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:704-708` filters the native inventory before the resolver ever sees it:

    if (record.kind === 'mcp' && !isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, {

`mcpServerRecords` emits "One qualified inventory record per declared MCP server (never one per file)" (native-sources.ts:472), so this runs per project `.mcp.json` server, in a trusted project, and drops denied ones. It is a real approve/reject list — managed `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` (`managed-policy.ts:1573`) — and it matches on transport/url/command identity, not just name, with the comment citing `managed-mcp.md:150` precisely so "a denied server cannot escape by being renamed." Claude's own `disabledMcpjsonServers: ["filesystem"]` example is reproducible today as a managed `deniedMcpServers` entry. The finding asserts an absence in the same subsystem where the mechanism is enforced.

Two further inaccuracies: (a) the gate is PROJECT trust (`ProjectTrustStore`, keyed by ProjectKey + root-identity fingerprint, `capabilities/project-trust-store.ts`), not "whole-workspace trust" — a separate workspace `trust-store.ts` exists and naming it is the wrong subsystem; (b) trust is not granted blind — `capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:105-129` reports the `.mcp.json` server SLUGS by name pre-trust ("the visibility half of the detect+consent model"), so the user sees the exact server list before approving.

That paragraph is about the PLUGIN subsystem — `set-capability-enabled` needs pluginKey+capabilityId (`plugins/management-service-v2.ts:283`) and reaches only plugin-owned servers; `setBuiltinDpMcpServerEnabled` reaches only built-in dp rows. A native `.mcp.json` row in the unified panel renders no switch at all (`McpServersPanel.tsx:294-297` → `onToggle` is null → `:352` renders nothing). So that "we are ahead" note does not cover this finding — but it is also not the reason the finding fails; storage-runtime.ts:704 is.

correctedState:
A narrower, true version of this row is worth re-filing; the row as written must not be acted on, because it would add gating on top of gating that already exists.

WHAT IS THERE: project `.mcp.json` servers pass two gates. (1) Whole-PROJECT trust — `native-sources.ts:995` (`projectTrustState === 'trusted'`), granted after `project-contribution-detect.ts` shows the user the declared server slugs by name. (2) A per-server managed allow/deny filter over each individual server record — `storage-runtime.ts:704-716` calling `isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, { name, ...mcpServerIdentity })`, i.e. Claude's own `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` from `managed-mcp.md`, enforced on url/command identity so a rename cannot evade it.

WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING, and its two bounds: the USER-tier half. Claude's `enabledMcpjsonServers`/`disabledMcpjsonServers`/`enableAllProjectMcpServers` are settable at user/project/local scope; our equivalent exists only at the MANAGED policy tier, so a user with no fleet policy has all-or-nothing project trust and no way to reject one server of a `.mcp.json` while accepting the rest. Second bound: the filter is skipped entirely off Pi — `storage-runtime.ts:632` `isPiCapabilityTurn = context.provider === 'pi'` and `:699` `if (!isPiCapabilityTurn) return true` — the same bound already recorded in the `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` addendum. There is likewise no post-trust per-server off switch: the unified MCP panel gives a native `.mcp.json` row no toggle, and `resolver.ts:1601-1613` plus `storage-runtime.ts:849-858` deliberately EXEMPT `kind === 'mcp'` from session selection ("R3 contract ... Do NOT widen this condition to `kind === 'mcp'` without changing that decided contract") — so any fix must change that decided contract explicitly rather than by side effect.
